title: He prayed… and that confuses people.
paragraphs: He prayed… and that confuses people.
If Jesus is God… why is He talking to God?
When Jesus Christ prays, like in John 17, He looks up and says, “Father…” — not as a performance, not as confusion, but as relationship.
Because God is not a lonely being.

The Father is God.
The Son (Jesus) is God.
The Holy Spirit is God.
But distinct Persons in perfect unity.
And that’s where many people miss it.
“In the beginning was the Word… and the Word was God.” (John 1:1)
But when Jesus came to earth, He didn’t stop being God—He added humanity.
The eternal love between the Father and the Son.
A relationship that existed before creation.
“Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.” (John 17:5)
But here’s the part that hits the heart.
Jesus didn’t just pray because He could.
He prayed because He chose dependence.
Even as God the Son, walking as a man, He modeled what we refuse to do:
“Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from Me… yet not My will, but Yours be done.” (Matthew 26:39)
So why does Jesus talk to the Father?
Because within the Trinity, there is real relationship, not roles being acted out.
Because as a man, He shows us how to live before God.
we are invited into that same relationship.
You don’t pray to a distant force.
is the same Jesus who went to the cross for your sin.
He made a way back to God.
You don’t have to wonder if God is listening.

If this opened your eyes, don’t keep it to yourself.
Someone you know is struggling with this exact question.
And maybe… they’re also waiting to meet the Father.
From confusion to clarity—because Jesus reveals everything.
